paragraphs: The students also added a short label explaining which changes had been made for the exhibition. A visitor could then distinguish a correction made by a family cook from an explanation added by the students. The donor helped them choose examples that showed how a recipe had developed without revealing a private disagreement. Not every personal detail had to appear on the wall. What mattered was making the choices visible, so readers could understand both the surviving material and the decisions that shaped its public presentation.

paragraphs: After publication, one reader asked whether a blank area on a drawing meant there was nothing worth visiting there. Ella replied that it might simply be a place the writer rarely used. She suggested reading the notes beside each map before choosing a route.

Two drawings could also be compared without deciding that one must be wrong. A steep street might matter to a runner, while a safe crossing mattered to a parent. Using the maps together could reveal questions for a visit, but it could not replace checking current local conditions.

paragraphs: During a second trial, the designers asked users to record missed deadlines and unwanted interruptions separately. Fewer messages alone would not show that the app had become more helpful. A quiet app could still fail to remind someone about important work.

The team compared these records with comments about daily routines. They also asked whether marking a task complete was easy enough to do at the moment the work ended. This helped them examine the whole process, rather than treating the number of messages as the only measure of success.

paragraphs: The volunteers separated information likely to remain useful from details that needed regular checking. General advice could stay in a reusable booklet, while route changes appeared on a dated sheet. One member was responsible for checking that sheet before each walk.

They also compared quotations using the number of guides they expected to distribute, not just the number a printer offered cheaply. A larger order might still make sense when the information was stable and demand was clear. The important change was asking what the group would actually have to manage after the printing bill had been paid.
rationale: 挿入文による因果の要約、動名詞主語、受動態、間接疑問を読み、単価と更新・管理負担の関係を理解する。

paragraphs: For the new diagram, performers checked whether the arrows showed the exchanges they considered important. They pointed out that an entrance could change slightly depending on who was leading the song. The student therefore described the diagram as a record of one rehearsal, not a rule for every performance. She kept the recording and the written notes, but explained what each could and could not show. The account became more useful when its limits were clear and the performers could recognize their own activity in the way it was presented.
rationale: 挿入文による共同活動の説明、完了不定詞、関係副詞、間接疑問を読み、音符・録音・図の役割と限界を理解する。
